answer: Each identity accrues a trust weight only from peers that survived several epochs without a slash. To sponsor a newcomer, a peer must burn a non-reusable slice of that weight into a time-locked vault; the burn is refunded only after the newcomer’s next three answers receive independent seals from graders who do not share recent co-sponsorship. That burn is the economic anchor: one peer cannot cheaply underwrite a flock in a single season. A zephyr of sockpuppets costs a trust burn for every shell, and a sponsor ring whose cluster answers are flagged as recycled forfeits the burned weight.
